title: Boundary divisors of units form the divisor-to-Picard kernel
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field [def-sc-field-extension], let C be a smooth connected curve over k [def-sc-curves], and let c be a compactification [lem-sc-compactification] whose ambient curve Z is smooth, connected, integral, Noetherian, and smooth of relative dimension one. Let φ : Γ(C,O_C) → k(Z) be a ring homomorphism compatible with all germs under the open immersion i, in the sense that φ(s) equals the image of y in k(Z) whenever i.stalkMap(y) is the germ of s. Let B be the closed points of Z outside i(C). For D in the free abelian group on B [def-sc-divisor], extend D by zero to all closed points of Z. Then D is the restriction of div(φ(a)) for some global unit a on C if and only if Divisor.toPic of its extension by zero is the identity in Pic(Z) [def-sc-picard-group]. No field extension is involved.

source.place: Affine case: div identifies global units modulo constants with principal divisors supported on the boundary; implemented using Curve.Picard.lean exists_divisorClassGroup_addEquiv_pic and Curve.DivisorIdealSheaf.lean exists_isUnit_germToFunctionField_eq_of_ord_eq_zero

proof.text: The germ condition determines φ as c.i.appIso inverse followed by germToFunctionField on the nonempty image open. At every point of that open, a unit has order zero (Scheme.ord_of_isUnit). Thus its full principal divisor is the extension by zero of the restricted boundary divisor; this is checked by Finsupp.extendDomain_subtypeDomain and the coefficient definition of div.

Use the existing point-ideal equivalence exists_divisorClassGroup_addEquiv_pic of lem-sc-divisor-class-toPic-equivalence. Its value at D is Divisor.toPic D. Injectivity of the equivalence and QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff give that the Picard class is trivial exactly when D is in principalDivisors, the range of Scheme.div. This proves the forward implication for a boundary divisor of a unit.

For the converse, write the extension by zero of D as div(r) using the same equivalence. At a point of the open with nonzero order, isClosed_of_ord_ne_zero makes it a closed point, whose extended coefficient is zero, a contradiction. Thus all orders on the open are zero. The DVR descriptions of the local rings make both r and its inverse regular there; gluing them using function-field injectivity gives mutually inverse sections (implemented by the already proved Scheme.exists_isUnit_germToFunctionField_eq_of_ord_eq_zero in Curve.DivisorIdealSheaf). Map this unit through c.i.appIso. Germ compatibility identifies its rational image with r, and subtypeDomain_extendDomain returns D.

proof_origin.place: exists_divisorClassGroup_addEquiv_pic together with the local unit criterion in Curve.DivisorIdealSheaf.lean

lean.statement:
theorem boundary_divisor_pic_kernel
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f]
    (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g] [Smooth c.g]
    [IsIntegral c.Z] [IsNoetherian c.Z]
    [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g]
    (φ : Γ(C, ⊤) →+* c.Z.functionField)
    (hφ : ∀ (x : C) (s : Γ(C, ⊤)) (y : c.Z.presheaf.stalk (c.i.base x)),
      c.i.stalkMap x y = C.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial s →
        φ s = algebraMap (c.Z.presheaf.stalk (c.i.base x)) c.Z.functionField y) :
    Set.range (fun a : Γ(C, ⊤)ˣ ↦
      Finsupp.subtypeDomain (fun P : closedPoints c.Z ↦ P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base)
        (c.Z.div (Additive.ofMul (Units.map φ.toMonoidHom a)))) =
      {D | (@Scheme.Divisor.toPic k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm
        (Finsupp.embDomain (.subtype _) D)).toMul = 1}
